Report written to `/tmp/probe/checks-style-warning.md` (1919 lines).

# checks-style-warning — established rules

## Output format (stderr), exact
```
<file>:<line>:<col>: <severity>: <message> [<id>]
<source line, each TAB → one space>
<(col-1) spaces>^
```
Secondary locations are extra 3-line blocks with severity token `note` and **no** `[id]` suffix; the primary location is normally repeated as the last note. Columns are **byte** offsets (UTF-8 not decoded), tabs count as 1. No line truncation. Source line otherwise echoed verbatim (leading spaces preserved).

`Checking <file> ...` goes to **stdout**. Multi-file adds `N/M files checked P% done` (integer truncation: 1/3→33%, 2/3→66%). Extra configs: `Checking dup.c: X=X...` (no space before `...`). `-q` kills all stdout. Exit 0 always unless `--error-exitcode=<n>` (then n) or bad args (1).

## Severity / enable model
| `--enable=` | turns on |
|---|---|
| *(none)* | `error` only |
| `style` | style **+ warning + performance + portability** |
| `warning` / `performance` / `portability` / `information` | that one only |
| `unusedFunction` | `unusedFunction` + `staticFunction` (both severity `style`) |
| `missingInclude` | `missingInclude` / `missingIncludeSystem` (severity `information`) |
| `all` | all of the above |

`--disable=<sev>` removes exactly one severity, applied **left-to-right in argv order** (`--enable=style --disable=all` → only error; reversed order → style on). `--disable=style` does NOT remove `unusedFunction`; `--disable=information` does NOT remove `missingInclude*` (separate flags). `--disable=all` accepted, exit 0.

`--enable=<check-id>` is **not** supported. Errors go to **stdout**, exit 1:
```
cppcheck: error: --enable parameter with the unknown name 'foo'
cppcheck: error: --disable parameter with the unknown name 'error'
cppcheck: error: --enable parameter is empty
```
Rejected names include `error`, `debug`, `internal`, `unusedVariable`. Comma lists work (`--enable=style,performance`); one bad element rejects the whole option.

`--enable=unusedFunction` → `sev.c:2:6: style: The function 'f' is never used. [unusedFunction]` (column = name token; emitted after all per-file checks).
`--enable=missingInclude` → `mi.c:1:2: information: Include file: "nope.h" not found. [missingInclude]` and `sev.c:1:2: information: Include file: <stdlib.h> not found. Please note: Standard library headers do not need to be provided to get proper results. [missingIncludeSystem]` (col always 2, emitted before analysis msgs). `--enable=information` alone does NOT emit them.

`information` adds a final 2-line (message + empty line, no caret) message:
```
nofile:0:0: information: Active checkers: 40/186 (use --checkers-report=<filename> to see details) [checkersReport]
```
Counts: C file — default/info/performance 40, portability 50, warning 73, style 112, all 113. C++ — default 60, style 172, all 173, all+inconclusive 183. Total always 186.

## --inconclusive
Inconclusive messages print `<sev>: inconclusive: <msg>` and are suppressed without `--inconclusive` — **except `bitwiseOnBoolean`, which always leaks through with the prefix**. Verified-gated: `duplicateBranch`, `constStatement`, `functionConst`, `initializerList`, `funcArgNamesDifferent`, `multiplySizeof`, `incompleteArrayFill`. `duplicateAssignExpression` fires without the flag and without the prefix despite being marked inconclusive in `--errorlist`. `--verbose` swaps `msg` for the `verbose` text.

## Ordering (byte-significant)
Grouped by check class, not by line: missingInclude* → CheckClass (uninitMemberVar, functionConst, noExplicitConstructor) → CheckCondition → CheckNullPointer → CheckOther (selfAssignment, unsignedLessThanZero, const*, variableScope, redundantAssignment, passedByValue, postfixOperator) → CheckString/Stl/Type → CheckUnusedVar in **three passes**: all `unusedStructMember`, then all `unreadVariable`, then all `unusedVariable`, then all `unassignedVariable` (each in declaration order) → `unusedFunction`/`staticFunction` (whole-program) → `checkersReport` last.

## Quirks to copy byte-for-byte
1. `redundantAssignInSwitch` notes contain the literal unexpanded `$symbol`: `note: $symbol is assigned` / `note: $symbol is overwritten` (plain `redundantAssignment` correctly says `a is assigned`).
2. `noOperatorEq`: `... does not have a operator= which is recommended ...` ("a", not "an").
3. `missingOverride`: `... is not marked with a 'override' specifier.`
4. `unusedPrivateFunction` emits **two identical** notes at the same location.
5. `comparisonError` uses literal `X`: `Expression '(X & 0x4) == 0x3' is always false.`; `mismatchingBitAnd`: `Result is always 0 (X = Y & 0xf0; Z = X & 0xf; => Z=0).` (`0x0f`→`0xf`).
6. Two `knownConditionTrueFalse` texts: `The comparison 'x == 5' is always true.` (spaces, period) vs `Condition 'i+1<i' is always false` (no spaces, no period).
7. No trailing period: `duplicateCondition`, `moduloofone`, `shadow*`, `cstyleCast`, `dangerousTypeCast`, `uselessOverride`, `constParameter*`/`constVariable*`, `funcArgOrderDifferent`, `shiftNegativeLHS`, `exceptThrowInDestructor`, `identicalConditionAfterEarlyExit`, `unusedPrivateFunction`, `unusedVariable` (`Unused variable: a`).

## Key message templates (verified)
`Variable 'X' is assigned a value that is never used.` unreadVariable · `Unused variable: X` unusedVariable · `Variable 'X' is not assigned a value.` unassignedVariable · `struct|class|union member 'C::m' is never used.` unusedStructMember · `The scope of the variable 'i' can be reduced.` variableScope · `Variable 'a' is reassigned a value before the old one has been used.` (+` 'break;' missing?` in switch) · `Variable 'n' is assigned an expression that holds the same value.` · `Redundant initialization for 'a'. The initialized value is overwritten before it is read.` (only with non-constant initializer) · `Redundant assignment of 'a' to itself.` selfAssignment · `Same expression on both sides of 'OP'.` / `Same expression in both branches of ternary operator.` [duplicateExpressionTernary] / `Opposite expression on both sides of 'OP'.` · `Clarify calculation precedence for '*' and '?'.` · `Suspicious condition (bitwise operator + comparison); Clarify expression with parentheses.` and `(assignment + comparison)` variants · `Boolean result is used in bitwise operation. Clarify expression with parentheses.` · `C-style pointer casting` · `Parameter 'p' can be declared as pointer to const` / `reference to const` / `const array`; `Variable 'p' can be declared as ...` · `Function parameter 'b' should be passed by const reference.` (performance) · `Prefer prefix ++/-- operators for non-primitive types.` · `Member variable 'A::y' is not initialized in the constructor.` / `... in the copy constructor.` / uninitDerivedMemberVar adds `Maybe it should be initialized directly in the class Bb?` · `Class 'A' has a constructor with 1 argument that is not explicit.` · `The class 'X' does not declare a constructor although it has private member variables which likely require initialization.` (col 1:1) · `Technically the member function 'A::getX' can be const.` · `The member function 'F::unused' can be static.` · `Virtual function 'init' is called from constructor 'E()' at line 3. Dynamic binding is not used.` · `Assigning a pointer to an integer is not portable.` / `Assigning an integer to a pointer is not portable.` (not for `long long`) · `Returning an address value in a function with integer return type is not portable.` · `int result is assigned to long variable. If the variable is long to avoid loss of information, then you have loss of information.` (severity **style**).

`comparisonOfBoolWithBoolError`, `assignBoolToFloat`, `constVariable` (non-array) require C++. `staticFunction` requires `--enable=unusedFunction`.

## Library dependency (critical)
With the stub `cfg/std.cfg`, all container/std-function checks are inert: `stlSize`, `stlIfFind/stlIfStrFind`, `useStlAlgorithm`, `knownEmptyContainer`, `containerOutOfBounds`, `sameIteratorExpression`, `uselessCallsEmpty`, `stlcstr*`, `redundantCopy*`, `argumentSize`, `mallocOnClassWarning`, `checkCastIntToCharAndBack`, `ignoredReturnValue`, `signConversion`, `passedByValue` for `std::string`. Pattern-only checks still work (`uselessCallsSubstr`, `memsetZeroBytes`, `incompleteArrayFill`, `sizeof*`, `memsetClassFloat`). Bad `--library` file → stdout `cppcheck: Failed to load library configuration file 'x.cfg'. Bad attribute value`, exit 1.

## Machine-readable catalogues (both dumped in the report)
- `--errorlist` (stdout, exit 0) = 338 ids with `severity`, `msg`, `verbose`, `cwe`, `inconclusive="true"`. Histogram: warning 108, style 94, error 92, portability 20, performance 19, information 5. Full per-severity id lists are in §10.
- `--checkers-report=<f>` = 186 checkers with `Yes  `/`No   ` + name padded to col 58 + `require:<unmet tokens>` (`style warning performance portability inconclusive c c++ c++03 c++11 c99 safeChecks windows-platform`). Severity tokens are **OR**. Never activatable from CLI here: `CheckClass::checkUnsafeClassRefMember` (safeChecks), `CheckOther::checkInterlockedDecrement` (windows-platform), `CheckStl::size` (c++03). Full 186-row activation matrix across all `--enable` values is in §11.
